title: Backdoor Attacks on Speech Emotion Recognition via TTS-Generated Poisoning
abstract: arXiv:2606.21052v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) systems increasingly leverage self-supervised acoustic representations, yet their vulnerability to training-time attacks remains largely underexplored. This paper presents the first systematic study of poisoning-based backdoor attacks on SER, with a focus on threats enabled by text-to-speech (TTS) generated audio. We introduce a stealthy, low-energy acoustic trigger that can be embedded imperceptibly into both natural and synthetic speech, enabling scalable and consistent poisoning. Our experiments demonstrate that SER models can be reliably compromised with high attack success rates under low poisoning ratios, while maintaining near-clean performance on benign inputs. We further show that backdoor patterns exhibit strong cross-model transferability and that self-supervised representations are particularly susceptible to learning these triggers. tldr: 本文首次系统研究了针对语音情感识别系统的后门投毒攻击，提出一种可隐蔽嵌入自然及TTS合成语音的低能量声学触发器，证明在低投毒比例下即可高成功率攻破模型，且后门具有强跨模型可迁移性，自监督表示尤其易受影响。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first systematic study of backdoor poisoning attacks on speech emotion recognition, introducing a stealthy low-energy acoustic trigger embeddable in both natural and TTS-generated speech, showing that models can be reliably compromised at low poisoning rates with strong cross-model transferability of the backdoors.
